### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via IAIService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via IAIService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d2814d3d46202a9a11cbd197a2b9f36118e75a55` — the merge of head `9c43ec77c19c4045ba649605673d462edefe2f34` into base `6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d2814d3d46202a9a11cbd197a2b9f36118e75a55 && git checkout d2814d3d46202a9a11cbd197a2b9f36118e75a55
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e 9c43ec77c19c4045ba649605673d462edefe2f34 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e && git merge --no-ff 9c43ec77c19c4045ba649605673d462edefe2f34

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:spec#2 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUe9c6YdtNkrzUnMUd

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9c43ec77c19c4045ba649605673d462edefe2f34`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts + ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useHitlInChat.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/ChatbotEnhanced.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/AiPendingActionsInbox.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useAiApprovalsTranslation.ts

Inputs: card #31884 (body, triage 6737259772, claim 6738283767, os-dev-report 6739673808), PR #31921 (body, 25-file list, net diff against the merge base 6a8f4151), and the 67 check-runs on this head (58 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed, none running). The check-run conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run here. Isolated sub-agent review on the schema face (`reviewFace` hits: the two spec paths above). The rest of the diff (both spec test files, the four plugin-chatbot test files, the eleven locale packs, the regenerated protocol.mdx, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `PendingActionStatus` (ai-service.ts:527) widens from five members to six, `held` placed between `approved` and `executed`. RIGHT: a widening of a published type, read by `PendingActionRow.status` (:548) and the `listPendingActions` filter (:504), neither of which needed a change.
- `IAIService.approvePendingAction` (ai-service.ts:483) returns `status: 'executed' | 'held' | 'failed'`. RIGHT: an implementer may now answer `held`; an existing implementer answering the old two still compiles. The type pin `ApproveOutcomeIsExecutedHeldOrFailed` in ai-service.test.ts holds the exact union.
- `AiPendingActionStatusSchema` (protocol.zod.ts:4157) gains `held`, so the row's `status`, the list route's `status` filter and `ListAiPendingActionsRequestSchema` all accept it. RIGHT, and protocol.test.ts pins `held` on the enum, the list filter and the approve response.
- `ApproveAiPendingActionResponseSchema.status` (protocol.zod.ts:4211) becomes `executed | held | failed`. RIGHT; the `rejected` refusal on this schema is kept and still pinned. The `result` describe now names the hold payload; `error` stays failed-only. RIGHT.
- Both mirrors say the same thing in the same words: `held` is not final, the host that held it writes `executed`, `rejected` or `failed`. The contract and the wire agree sentence by sentence (ai-service.ts:471-478 and :519-526 against protocol.zod.ts:4151-4156 and :4204-4210).
- `api-surface/` does not move: it lists export names only (api.json:30-31, :81-82; contracts.json:253), and no export was added, removed or renamed. RIGHT. `authorable-surface/` lists key paths (`api/ApproveAiPendingActionResponse:status`), not enum values, so the `Metadata-protocol: none` baseline rule is not touched. RIGHT. No committed JSON under packages/spec carries the enum values; the one stale generated artefact, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, is regenerated in the diff and Build Docs is green.
- `ToolDecisionState` (ChatbotEnhanced.tsx:1060) gains a `held` member. This is a published type (plugin-chatbot index.tsx:308 and useHitlInChat.ts:8 re-export it), so a host switching on `state` exhaustively gets a new case. RIGHT to declare (acceptance note 3); a widening in a UI package, `patch` under the lockstep group.
- Consumer reach, judged against the live tree, not the PR body: every in-repo site that branches on the pending-action status or the approve outcome is in the diff. useHitlInChat.ts:255-282 (the `held` branch now sits before the catch-all that used to record it as `success`), ChatbotEnhanced.tsx:3313-3348 (generic strip) and :3683-3713 (record-write card), AiPendingActionsInbox.tsx:117-124 (variant), :144-151 (badge), :268-276 (approve outcome). `usePendingActions.ts` types `ApproveOutcome` as the spec type (:109) and widens with it. `mapMessages.ts` reads only the tool's `pending_approval` envelope; app-shell `useChatConversation.ts:330` synthesises that envelope and never reads the approve outcome; `AiChatPage.tsx` passes decisions through. `packages/client/src/index.ts:7567` passes the response through untyped-switch-free. No consumer under apps/. The dev's reach claim is confirmed.
- Read, not reviewed (outside the diff): the client SDK's `approve()` docblock (packages/client/src/index.ts:7562-7565) still warns about `failed` as the only 200 that is not a write; `held` is now a second. A follow-up on `@objectstack/client`, not this PR.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset .changeset/31884-pending-action-held.md: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`, `@object-ui/i18n`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the changeset and the PR body. Check Changeset is green on this head.
- Dev deviation 1 (patch, not the claim's minor): JUDGED RIGHT. AGENTS.md rule 3 and the Check Changeset prose make the level follow the Metadata-protocol kind alone, and `none` covers "REST, drivers, services". `PendingActionStatus` is a service contract (triage 6737259772: not authorable shape) and `AiPendingActionStatusSchema` is a REST wire enum; neither is something a metadata author writes, so `added` would have been the wrong kind. The claim's `minor` beside `none` was the claim's own inconsistency, and the dev resolved it on the side the rule names. A widening that is not a protocol change ships `patch` and keeps its `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line, which is what the changeset does.
- Dev deviation 2 (`@object-ui/i18n` patch): JUDGED RIGHT. The package is a published member of the fixed group (.changeset/config.json:96, version 18.3.0, not private) and the diff moves its source in eleven packs, so a changeset entry is owed, and `patch` follows `none`.
- Clause-②: `yes (widening)` is the right arm: two published accept sets (the status enum and the approve-outcome enum) grow and nothing is refused that was accepted before.

### ③ Boundary flags

- "changeset is patch, not minor": answered above, accepted.
- "`@object-ui/i18n` is touched and carries its own patch": answered above, accepted.
- "no app-shell file changed": CONFIRMED in the tree. useChatConversation.ts has no branch on the approve outcome; its only status literal is the synthesised `pending_approval` envelope (:330).
- "zh-Hans 审批中 and ja 承認者の承認待ち": accepted. Both packs already spend the plain waiting words on `statusPending` (zh-Hans:4283 待审批, ja:4075 承認待ち), so the held label is worded apart, as the PR says. The en string is the card's mandated "Waiting for approval".
- `Skills-docs: none`: CONFIRMED. The only skill naming the queue is skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:162-169, which teaches the `pending_approval` envelope, the inbox and the routes and never enumerates status values; its "whether your action is held" is the ordinary word, about the skip rule, not this enum. No ADR or hand-written doc enumerates the statuses (content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx:74 names `IAIService` in a one-row table only). No skills child is owed.
- Out-of-scope finding "inbox Decided tab lists held rows" (acceptance note 4): JUDGED an accepted deviation, graded nit below. The Decided tab is `status !== 'pending'` (AiPendingActionsInbox.tsx:257-258) and the Approve / Reject buttons are keyed on `status === 'pending'` (:421), so a held row shows its "Waiting for approval" badge with no buttons. From the member's side the decision is made and the wait is someone else's, so Decided is not wrong, and the card's done-list (item 3) asks only that no consumer shows success. Whether a Held tab is wanted is a product call for the seat; if it wants one, a `domain:ui` follow-up card, not this PR.
- Out-of-scope finding "cloud records held instead of executed": escalated as the card already does (triage 6737259772: cloud is the consumer, its own follow-up). No cloud code here, as ruled.
- Acceptance note 2 (no continuation turn on `held`): accepted. `buildContinuationPrompt` (useHitlInChat.ts:333-365) returned nothing for `held` before this PR, so behaviour is unchanged; telling the model the write is held would be new behaviour the card does not ask for. Noted for the cloud follow-up: once a host resolves a held action, nothing in the chat learns the final state. That is the seam the card names, not a defect here.
- `open_questions`: none declared, none found.
- Human Minimum item 8 unchecked: the body carries the lane's Chinese reader block by rule; the title and the rest are English. Not a contract matter.

### ④ Design judgment

packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts: judged against the card's problem statement and its first consumer in the diff. The widening does what the card asks and no more: `held` is defined as accepted-then-waiting, not final, with the host that held it named as the writer of the final state, and `approvePendingAction` is allowed to return it with the hold payload as `result`. Tried to break it: a `held` row cannot be approved again through this service (the row is not `pending`, and the contract gives this service no move out of `held`), a reject route never yields `held`, and an implementer that answers only the old two still satisfies the type. Holds.

packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts: judged against the contract it mirrors and against `usePendingActions.ts`, its first consumer. The enum order and wording match the contract; the approve response gains `held` and keeps the `rejected` refusal; the list filter accepts `held` so an inbox can ask for held rows. Holds.

Implementing files, each read against the contract sentence by sentence:
- useHitlInChat.ts:275-281: `held` gets its own state, `decision: 'approved'` (only the approve route can answer it), `result` carried, `succeeded` left false so no continuation turn, and `onDecided` still receives the raw payload. Agrees.
- ChatbotEnhanced.tsx:3313-3348 and :3683-3713: both cards draw an hourglass and the borrowed inbox label for `held`, never the OK or written line; `isAwaitingApproval` (:3187-3188) is false once any decision exists, so the buttons go away. The hourglass import pre-exists on main. Agrees.
- AiPendingActionsInbox.tsx:117-124, :144-151, :268-276, :352-358: badge, variant and the approve outcome all read `held` as waiting, not executed and not failed. Agrees.
- useAiApprovalsTranslation.ts:64: the provider-less fallback row mirrors the en pack, and the noProviderFallback test's key list is extended with it. Agrees.

Findings:
- must-fix: none.
- should-fix: none.
- nit, protocol.zod.ts:4171 and :4177: the row schema's describes still read `Serialized result, once executed` and `Actor that approved or rejected it`; a `held` row may now carry the hold payload in `result` with the member as `decided_by`. Description text only, no accept-set effect. Fixing it moves the head, so left as an accepted deviation; fold into the next spec PR that touches this block.
- nit, ai-service.ts:468-469: the opening sentence "Updates the row to `executed` (or `failed`)" is left above the paragraph that adds the third outcome. Reads fine, but the two could be one sentence. Accepted deviation.
- nit, ChatbotEnhanced.tsx:1060: the `held` member carries `message?` that nothing writes (useHitlInChat.ts:281 sets none) and nothing reads (both renders use the label). Harmless slack in a published type; accepted deviation.
- nit, AiPendingActionsInbox.tsx:257-258: held rows list under Decided with no buttons (acceptance note 4). Accepted deviation; a product call for the seat, follow-up card if a Held tab is wanted.

Nits alone: the round ends on this head. Must-fix cards owed: none.

domain:spec#2 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUe9c6YdtNkrzUnMUd

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：AI 待审批动作新增一个状态 `held`（等待审批）。成员在对话里确认了一次 AI 写入后，如果企业策略把它拦下、转给对话外的审批人，这条记录不再写成「已执行」。聊天卡片和审批收件箱都会显示「等待审批」，而不是成功。改动包括契约 `IAIService`、REST 的两处枚举镜像、plugin-chatbot 里三个读取状态的地方，以及 11 个语言包。
- 为什么改：契约原来只允许 `executed` 或 `failed` 两种结果。cloud 的企业写入拦截只能把还没写入的数据记成「已执行」，于是账本、聊天卡片和所有按状态分支的消费者，都会把一次没发生的写入当成已完成。
- 风险与回滚：只放宽不收紧，旧的 `executed` / `failed` 答复照常解析和显示。本仓库里没有 `approvePendingAction` 的实现，真正返回 `held` 的是 cloud 的后续卡；在那之前，界面上不会出现新状态。回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`（状态和返回值的说明，包括谁把 `held` 推进到终态）；`ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useHitlInChat.ts`（`held` 不再落入成功分支）。
- 两分钟验证：`cd ui && pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/useHitlInChat.test.tsx`，应全绿。
- 需要你做的：无。本 PR 不属受管面，契约复核已通过，由本席落地。
- 席位意见：建议合。CI 全绿；契约复核 PASS，没有应改项，只有四条 nit。复核逐个核对了状态枚举在本仓库的所有消费者，都已处理 `held`，没有一处把它显示成成功。

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · 2026-11-09T12:44Z · head `9c43ec77c19c4045ba649605673d462edefe2f34`

Seat `domain:spec#2` reviewed the diff of its own dispatch: claim 6738283767 on #31884, card thread `session_01QsR2jQmF8zoS2dZmdtH5cp`, report 6739673808. Checked against GitHub, not against the report.

1. **Shape**
   - 25 files, +284 / -37, under the 3000 threshold.
   - Draft, base `main`, and the body opens with `Fixes #31884`.
   - Spec:
     - `contracts/ai-service.ts` adds `held` to `PendingActionStatus` and to the approve return;
     - `api/protocol.zod.ts` mirrors it in the status enum (row, list filter) and in the approve response;
     - tests are updated, and `protocol.mdx` is regenerated.
   - UI: `useHitlInChat.ts` (a held branch ahead of the success catch-all), `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx` (both card kinds), `AiPendingActionsInbox.tsx`, `useAiApprovalsTranslation.ts`, one key in each of the 11 locale packs, and tests.
   - One changeset: `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` and `@object-ui/i18n`, all patch.
   - Every file is inside the claim. `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` is clean.
2. **Premise**
   - It held at claim time and still holds on this head. On `main`, `PendingActionStatus` has no non-terminal decided member, so a host-held write can only be recorded as `executed` (the repo:cloud finding the card was filed from, triage 6737259772).
3. **Gates and check-runs**
   - On this head: 67 runs, 58 success, 9 skipped, 0 red.
   - `check-expected-skips --pr 31921`: OK, every skip is in main's roster (exit 0).
4. **Accepted deviations**
   - **Patch, not minor.** The claim named minor. The changeset level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone, and `none` is right for a service contract and a REST enum. `check-changeset-no-major` refuses minor beside `none`. The reviewer judged this right. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` stands.
   - **The `@object-ui/i18n` patch** is right: it is a published fixed-group member whose source moved.
   - **Held rows list under the inbox's Decided tab.** Decided is `status !== 'pending'`. The member has decided, and the row shows the waiting badge with no buttons. A separate Held tab would be a product call for domain:ui, not this card's.
   - **Four nits** from the review are accepted as written; they ride the next touch of these files:
     - two descriptions in `protocol.zod.ts` (L4171, L4177) still word the row as executed or rejected;
     - the opening sentence of the approve docblock in `ai-service.ts` (L468) still names only executed or failed;
     - an unused `message?` on the held `ToolDecisionState` member;
     - the Decided-tab listing above.
5. **Out of scope and Skills-docs**
   - `Skills-docs: none` is confirmed: `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` teaches the approval envelope, the inbox and the routes, never the status values.
   - The `@objectstack/client` `approve()` docblock (`packages/client/src/index.ts` L7562) names only `failed` as the non-write 200. It was read, not reviewed, and is left for the next client touch.
   - The cloud implementation that returns `held` belongs to repo:cloud's follow-up.
6. **Landing**
   - `check-governed-merges --pr 31921`: NOT governed (0 of 25 paths hit the register).
   - `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
   - Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`: PASS, record 6740342689 on this head, written by an isolated Fable reviewer and adopted by this seat under the maintainer's 2026-11-08 rule.
   - This seat flips the PR ready and arms auto-merge. On merge, `Fixes` closes #31884, and this seat posts the landing note.
